note: The go-to staple order ("아아" in casual slang).
Mugs or reusable cups are required for dine-in drinks.
Can also say 테이크아웃 (takeout) at the counter.
Swap 적게 for 많이 to ask for extra ice.

english: Can I swap to oat milk?
note: Useful for dietary swaps or decaf (디카페인).
Often printed near the bottom of your paper receipt.
Reply after "영수증 드릴까요?" (Would you like a receipt?).
Some cafés print the keypad code on your receipt.
Answer to "아이스로 드릴까요, 따뜻한 걸로 드릴까요?" (Iced or hot?).
Many Seoul cafés are cashless (현금 없는 매장) and accept cards or mobile pay.
Useful for evening café visits; expect a ~500 KRW surcharge at some chains.
Works for lattes, ades (에이드), and milk teas; say 시럽 빼고 for no syrup.

english: Please add an extra espresso shot
note: Say 투 샷 추가 to add two shots; 연하게 해 주세요 asks for a milder brew.

english: What is your signature drink here?
note: Specialty roasters often highlight unique cream lattes (아인슈페너 / 크림라떼).
Helpful when cafés separate ordering kiosks from the pickup counter.

english: Come pick up when the buzzer rings
note: Common staff phrase; return the buzzer (진동벨) when collecting your tray.

english: Please put them in a drink carrier
note: Ask for 빨대 (straw) or 냅킨 (napkin) at the pickup counter if not self-serve.

english: Are there seats with power outlets?
note: Check wall signs—some busy cafés restrict outlet use or laptop hours.

korean: 빵 좀 데워 주실 수 있나요?
romanization: ppang jom dewo jusil su innayo?
english: Could you warm up this pastry?
note: Works for croissants, scones, or bagels; self-serve toaster ovens are common too.

english: Please put it in my tumbler
note: Most Korean chains offer a 300–500 KRW eco discount for personal cups.
Check 마지막 주문 (last order) time—often 30 minutes before closing.
Chain cafés often use 레귤러 (regular), 라지 (large), or 벤티 (venti).
Many cafés have a self-serve water station near the pickup bar.
